content.overview: Outsiders may assume that internal proceedings have been properly followed, unless they had notice or the act was ultra vires.
content.glance: Outsiders may assume that internal proceedings have been properly followed, unless they had notice or the act was ultra vires.
content.study: Indoor management and constructive notice. Outsiders may assume that internal proceedings have been properly followed, unless they had notice or the act was ultra vires. The section applies only to the persons, companies, and transactions it names. A filing, approval, or penalty arises only where the section or a rule under it says so. It does not create a power that is reserved to another section or to the Tribunal. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Principle
sections.body: Outsiders may assume that internal proceedings have been properly followed, unless they had notice or the act was ultra vires.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: Constructive notice of registered documents limits the Turquand rule. Suspicion, forgery, and acts outside apparent authority defeat the protection. The doctrine does not validate a breach of a mandatory section, because s. 6 overrides inconsistent internal acts.

caseLaw.name: Royal British Bank v Turquand
caseLaw.point: A person dealing with a company in good faith may assume that internal procedures have been complied with. The rule does not protect a person who knows of the irregularity.
